codeReviewIssues.description: Two separate subscribeToType('queue:step-started', ...) handlers are registered in the same pipelineUnsubs array — one for queue progress tracking and one for sprint iteration tracking. While functionally correct (EventBus supports multiple subscribers), combining them into a single handler would be cleaner and avoid the mild confusion of two handlers for the same event type.

The e2e test 'tests/e2e/sprint-pipeline.sh' detect_sprint_state() function greps for system messages like 'Sprint started', 'Sprint completed', 'Sprint escalating' which were previously emitted by the OpenTUI adapter's sprint:* event handlers (now removed). These patterns will no longer match during live sprint runs. The telemetry bar 'Sprint N/M' pattern still works, and the script falls through to standard pipeline state detection, so this is unlikely to cause false failures — but the sprint-specific detection paths are now dead code in the e2e script.

Headless adapter sprint label detection relies on stepTitle containing the substring 'Sprint' (case-sensitive) to append '(sprint iteration)' label. If the sprint queue template's step title format ever changes (e.g., lowercase 'sprint'), the headless adapter would silently stop labeling sprint work steps. A more robust approach would be to pass a flag or use stepType-based detection consistently (like verify steps already do).

summary: Clean, well-executed feature. sprint-loop.ts and createSprintStageLoop adapter deleted, all 6 sprint:* event types removed from events/types.ts, event-bus.ts, and all 3 adapters (opentui, headless, mock). Shared types extracted to sprint/types.ts with import updates across 4 files. Sprint iteration tracking re-wired through queue:step-started events in flywheel-shell.tsx with verify-step-based sprint detection. Headless adapter enhanced with sprint context labels. 42 tests cover all expected behaviors. Only minor observations: dual queue:step-started subscription, stale e2e script patterns, and one string-matching fragility in headless adapter.
